Content: People are supported through rituals and relationships to grieve, feel rage, process pain and also celebrate, embody joy and healing. When faced with conflict or harm has occurred, we develop the skills to be in discomfort with one another and repair harm and continue to tend to our relationships. The human toolkit includes care and resolution of conflict, not escalation and harm done to one another at the individual level or beyond. We are not scared to disagree because we know that we are safe. We are not scared of grief or rage because we keep one another safe. We know that disagreeing, showing anger and sadness is what tests our relationships and strengthens our deepest bonds. We practice seeking out, receiving, and giving accountability as an act of love. We know this is necessary for community growth and development. We practice being in right relationship with land, water, self, each other, death, and spirit. We are communities of deep listeners. We hear into story and also receive the gifts of wisdom and sound advice.

When things are difficult, we forgive. Our friends, neighbors, and even acquaintances show up to help us. We know how to hold each other's hearts with care. Courage self-perpetuates and cross-pollinates. Our joys and our sorrows are shared wholly (not in pictures validated with double clicks). When we want to reconnect with someone we speak to them and see their eyes (this includes our ancestors who we collectively acknowledge are with us always). We heal pain and suffering passed down through our bodies by spending more time laughing with our children on our laps. We connect at a macro level, acknowledging our ability to self-govern and determine how we fit into the biggest webs and spaces. We let go of braining our way through problems that we created and instead anchor to our bodies and land and water and the things that are true and not

While we are trained in self and community defense, when or if there is conflict - it is rooted and active with principles and values. And when someone moves without principle, we know how to respond.

We still have weapons, but guns are banned, and no more bullets are made. All the metals have to be used for other needs: housing, construction... production is decided by people, who live where production is made.

While the weapons have been secured, the places those weapons were deployed have found avenues towards healing. What does this mean? The island of Vieques brings delegations of travelers to marvel at how they have repaired the land, found ways to sustainably grow foods, and found ways to center industries that are supporting other communities of people to repair and heal from war.
Artists and growers continue to repurpose rusted shells of ammunition and weapons to make living art, that reminds of the pains of the past but point towards a new way
We practice restorative justice with purpose.
Intelligence is evidenced by problem solving, tenacity in the face of challenge, willingness to take a risk and ask a question.
What gets tended to include what children learn, helping people work through conflicts and interrupting anger.

We help each other practice turning toward, listening, and sitting with difference. We learn therapeutic stances - all of us. We don't confine relationships to legal bonds, there is flowing together and choosing how to be in connection.
Peace is stasis. There's not a word for it because it's everywhere.

We've come to embrace that some conflict is natural. We dont love it but just as some of us still don't like the smell of eucalyptus, we know it is healthy and we learn to see it as generative soul medicine
This came about through innovation and creativity and discipline. It involved breaking with purity.

We had to agree to use some of the bad processes to get us to the new. But we didn't do that in an enabling or light way. We put focus. We knew what was harmful. And we new the care that needed to be taken as we turned the tide.

Conflict is generative; meaning laughing - crying - debates - with people hugging and thinking for hours after. Resolution can be more than one thing; We ask youth and elders when we get stuck on where to plant crops. We listen to long stories to help us find our way toward a "decision" And we are okay if it does not work out. We laugh, cry, and find a new place to plant.
Reparations only after public acknowledgement of harm. Co-design of accountability through service. Reciprocity.
things that were used for violence are cleaned and repurposed. They are lessons and teachers from the past. New life.

Book depots are governed by arc steward storytellers whose job it is to make sure that everybody has access to the stories and that the stories in the oral tradition that are captured and are woven together. Arc Stewards guide the Al librarians who are cataloging the stories and can pull them up for conflict healing processes that ground people in past, present, and future stories.
Most causes for war are eliminated and violence is funneled into localized and global constructs wherein both outlet and repair are held in equal emphasis.
We have learned during breaking points how to collaborate and equalize in our solutions, and continue to learn to do that throughout lifespans.
There is a unity that honors difference. The conflicts that emerge now come from disagreements in strategy but not rooted in judgements of character or identity - it's not personal.

There are still cascades of weapons stored somewhere. But where they are is secured with the greatest of care. The most dangerous and toxic of weapons have been as deconstructed as the science and art of the day allow. The places that hold these kinds of items are not museums - where warfare and violence is celebrated. They are left to be cared for.
Guns and weapons have literally been melted down to create the metal infrastructure of ecobuilding that finally ensured everyone had a home to go to.
We hold truth and reconciliation circles. Circle upon circle.

The nation state is no longer useful. Diaspora's coalesce around notions of affinity and exchange. The free movement of peoples globally. Tech facilitates major changes in energy production and distribution.
We are more local and global than we've ever been and incentives for war continue to be greatly reduced. Languages merge. FTL becomes possible and green.
When conflict arises, there is a council of people who are responsible for supporting conflict resolution that is rooted in love and trust.
Conflict is seen as an opportunity to deepen relationship, be curious about one another, and learn to make space for everything that’s coming up.

There are many people who collect the needs of the people. When there is conflict, their job is to sit with people and help each party absorb loss or appreciate the gain–to get to that sense that can only be felt that something is just–and that this is how it is now. The people with this responsibility are called makers. This was previously known as government.
Conflict exists, but we move slow enough to hold the difference, share grief, and repair the harm.
When harm happens we get to the understanding of the harm that was caused, and the way to restore that harm.

Restorative justice - will take us some time where there is  No armed force, police, keeping community “safe.” Hard to imagine a place where people don’t have guns. Community Council community circles - offered as invitation from when people are young, children from the beginning are invited to consider what accountability for themselves and each other looks like.
There wont be war
Laws exist to respond to harm
Original of Translation: Las leyes existen para responder al daño.

Content: When people cause harm to others, we focus on restorative justice. The harmed person is returned to the state they were in before the harm.
Original of Translation: Cuando la gente causa daño a otros, nos enfocamos en justicia restaurativa. La persona dañada regrese al estado antes del daño.

Content: We understand that sometimes the most amazing leaps forward in life come from the most difficult or hurtful things.

We hold people who have done something hurtful.  It’s an energetic thing in addition to the practicalities.  There are healers whose job is to hold people through the darkness until things are healed.  We are committed to holding people through their own changes and transformations.  This role is sacred.
Collective support and shared community. Abolish the criminal legal system and replace it with spaces to learn and grow and have access to do things differently in the future.

The truth and reconciliation process about colonization continues, in a new phase of the spiral that people imagined decades ago. People share grief, rage and love with each other about the arc their ancestors played parts in, and ancestral healing rituals are practiced with celestial guidance in all directions. Overlapping circles include people of all walks and ages, supporting their healing and wholing wherever their lineage and bodies are on their journey back to thriving interdependence.
Circle keeping is a path to conflict resolution.
Repair is a regular practice that young people are aware of and have familiarity with.

And there won't be incarceration and jailing and trapping and keeping and punishing.  It will be people surrounding someone that may have misstepped and will be counseled and helped in a loving way rather than in a punishing way, in an isolation and entrapment.  
 But to lift up this person that needs the lifting, and primarily in the way of just, I would say, spewing love.  Leaking love, spreading it, and living it and being it, and with recognition of where we came from, what it was, where we've come from, where have you come from to be in this place.

The council of elders listens to conflicts, trains to prevent the conflicts. We argue well by managing expectations. We have peer-to-peer learning so that the expertise is in the community without needing experts to come in.
Allotments transition to something more communal.
Conflict over values doesn’t compromise dignity. We disagree without being disagreeable. Money is not about enoughness because there is plenty. Conflict ends with breaking bread.

There is a witnessing and holding by the community if someone causes harm. The community identifies what was missing in the community for the person to have done what they did. Wrongdoing is composted so that something new can come forward. Every single soul is necessary.

Conflict arises and is resolved respecting humanism.
Art-making brings hopes of restoration and reconciliation.
Origami–creating something beautiful from something so simple.

We move through conflict with respect for every perspective, taking time and space to listen to each other, and being ok with not always having it how we think it should be. There is space to be at odds on the way to making decisions for the benefit of the community.
When a harm is committed, everyone involved gets together to share and talk about what happens next. There is effort to understand every side.

Conflict is resolved before there is conflict because community agreements are created before conversations, meetings, gatherings, etc... These agreements are adjusted and cared for as needed. Trust is rampant and all beings alive and inanimate are connected and know they are connected. When one of us hurts, we all hurt. This is literally felt and experienced, so resolving conflict before it begins is paramount to our thriving lives. The definition of peace has expanded and exemplified because all beings alive and inanimate feel peace and experience peace. This is possible because justice and liberation have been achieved. Deep listening and loving has transformed our brains and bodies into an energy that is shared and is ecstatic.
Conflict still happens.  The people who are involved in those conflicts plant seeds together and are responsible for the wellbeing of them.  They cultivate the tending together.
Conflict is resolved with curiosity. Questions are asked with compassion and empathy.

Conflict is resolved by dancing together. Leaders from all nations dance before all meetings, before any words are uttered. Dance happens at the end of all meetings and gatherings. Dance is the most common way of interacting together. With each other, with nature, with the built environment.
When we have emotional upsets or conflicts, we will have people we can be with or walk with to help hold and process what we are feeling

Date/Circle Name: 2/27/25 Redwood City and North Fair Oaks, CA Sobrato 2
Content: We have less conflict because all our base needs are met–including time.  We would have long ago learned to hear out our elders…etc.  The pressure of time has evaporated.

From the beginning everyone knows they are loved. Even if they do something wrong, they know they are loved and this way harm does not expand. Punishment ceases to blow up the hearts of those who are not met with love when they cause harm.

The process for reconciliation when someone has done harm involves truth in reconciliation processes, healers, and community  members with skills to move through the harm and healing together. There are rituals of joyful homecoming to welcome folks back after rituals to heal harm.

When there are conflicts we seek out differing perspectives which help us heal the conflicts collectively. If everyone in the same room agrees on something, then we know we must invite more people to bring more to the conversation, things that may otherwise be overlooked or minimized.
When harm is done, people work together to restore the balance that was lost. All participate in the healing because when someone is hurt, all are impacted.
Justice lives not in prisons but in community care. When harm happens, we restore balance together. Everyone participates in healing, because everyone is impacted.

Small harms are met with easy repair - offered and accepted.

Big harms are handled from a community perspective rather than a narrow focus on the individual.

We have space and processes that translate into shared norms and practices of mutual accountability. When individuals act in ways that they know impact the collective, we have ways that center repair and wholeness. We don’t separate. We surround.
The wise counsel at dusk and Elila knows she can trust them with their conflict. Friends all know that conflict can transition for good and are cheering her on.
Conflict is generative. Harm to the earth is considered an abomination.

We have companion intelligence that reflects back our collective intelligence. A love brigade shows up when someone causes harm so that they know they are loved and have love. Rooting in relationship is just the norm. We are not learning how to live, we are living, so there is spaciousness for building relationships.

The structures for holding accountability for people that have caused harm and support for those that have been harmed are separate. We understand that we hold the circumstances collectively for the harm and healing from it. One of the important institutions is remembrance. Regular enactment of the stories of how things came together. There is deep identification with both the parts of our history – that which made transformation possible and the parts that made it necessary. There is glory and possibility of life plus awareness of our capacity to bring back what we just came out of. Not from fear but a sense of responsibility to not go back. There is confidence that we know how to hold the most destructive undercurrents into their wise forms.
War is a memory
When harm occurs, individuals are held accountable by the community in a way that decenters punishment in a way that is defined by community.
Violence free
Maladaptive and harmful choices are judged by the need that led to that action and resources and repair are focused on meeting needs – fear, scarcity, self-worth.
Restorative justice is more common and used more often than prison. RJ is the go-to.
No penal system. Healing from trauma opportunities by serving the community in response.
Justice council of elders, restorative circles.
No penal system, the individual is not the mistake, it is the failure of society and society must welcome the person back into community.

Just as we ensure the kitchen is cleaned after a meal - we share in the tasks of maintaining the community. 

There can be conflict in the community, even crime. We practice restorative justice in ways that protect the victim and community, whoever experienced harm. For heinous crimes, we practice rehabilitation through positive proactive communities. 

We seek to address conflict in ways that heal and don’t ostracize. We interrupt patterns of violence.

Date/Circle Name: 10/30/25 Kailua, HI Kipuka Pala'a Group, Le Jardin Academy
Content: We heal generational trauma because we know working together will become our greatest strength and we no longer feel the need to raise our weapons to fight each other. We work together to upend systemic racism and classism and poverty and world hunger. To bring this future closer we made sure people no longer felt the need to fight one another. We all move forward with a shared understanding of each other’s thoughts, needs, and strengths.
Clear understanding role between confrontation and violence
More parks than prisons. How we offer accountability and care. Offer support and care. Compassionate and humane way of addressing and offering accountability.
If crime is still a reality, then justice is healing
Violence is outdated programming

The human brain has evolved to be able to make complex decisions under stress. Education is basic skill building, exploration, critical thinking and kids being taught about conflict and harm at a young age. Conflict is resolved by resolving the needs that are opposing, building from what we learn from when needs oppose. Harm is when we hurt another. Conflict is not seen as harm. If someone who causes harm is not willing to be accountable, there is a way of holding a boundary that relies on skilled boundary building – these are clearly defined and practiced. There is a constant invitation for someone who has caused harm to repair, and a constant boundary. We don’t pretend like conflict and harm don’t exist, but we have the skills – like algebra or physics – taught to kids.
There are multiple tiers of options for people to take different types of accountability. The repair role with people who have done really serious harm is coveted.

No genocides, militarization or war. Plants started to grow, poppies in Palestine. Children feel safe in blue skies (instead of fearful of drones). Borders are determined by care for natural life in places. There is no waste of natural resources. The water remembers. There is no Utopia – we remember all of this.
“Justice is what love looks like in public” quote is lived into.  When something goes wrong, the community instinctively surrounds and cares for no matter what the situation is.
When there is conflict, we understand that there is something to address with all of us.  We see tending to relationship as the key to everything we do.

We embrace conflict as an opportunity to connect..  You regularly hear things like, “I got in an argument with my neighbor that ended shitty - I can’t wait to see them tomorrow.  I can tell I have so much to learn.”  or “I just found out my child is being bullied.  Let’s go figure out what the bully needs so both of the can start healing now.
We see and know harm as a fracture in our collective wholeness, and therefore we reconcile by returning to wholeness–doubling down on love.

We view mistakes as opportunities to learn, teach, and do better. When we say we, we include all that is living and non-living. A world without conflict will evolve because future generations will get better at learning and applying lessons from the past. There are various languages and communication styles but we all understand each other.
When conflict or harm happens, as it always does, care and healing is offered.  Rather than “Who is to blame or what did they do?”, the question is “What need is unmet and how can we meet it?”

Our systems function because there are not threats of physical or psychological war. No class a war, because everyone is trained and explores how each human unit establishes and negotiates the systems that we exist in.
Non violent conflict resolution.

Since we look out for each other - we don’t have the same volume of misconduct and need much less punitive ways to approach difficulties and conflict. We see crime as a need for attention and care, and work to support the person and their community to show up well.
Community councils for when people are harmed vs. punishment

Peace and love, that’s the part that means something to me the most, as I seen a lot of racism, killings, hate crimes and so much more in person or online. AS I help or try to help my community, I wish my descendants do the same in an era of peace, love, unity and justice, like Community Coalition.
No gang violence.

We seek new ways to thrive, not survive. Our tools and systems enhance and improve our lives, not dictate them. Prison is nonexistent– just a distant memory and even unbelievable to think people lived in certain conditions. Now there is healing. It is a process that is rooted in human connection and interaction, finding commonalities humanizing the individual and their lived experience so they can have a sense of self and alleviating burdens through the practice of mutual aid.

Navigating conflict is seen and felt as an invitation for connection and closeness. We slow down, engage and connect. We speak honestly, transparently and with a collective vision of being in community with each other. Living in calmness and trust so that conflict can be resolved by voicing what is felt without judgment, rejection or resentment.

Human Life 
Who are you to take mine. 
No more guns, drugs, jails or prisons. Only help, support and love is given. Real  rehabilitation. 
No more lock you up and throw away the key. No more separation from families. No more toxic environments where your life will be spent.

Differences are celebrated, and not  feared, because people understand that unity grows stronger when everyone is  respected. This green world is not perfect. Challenges are still there, but instead  of fighting each other, people faced problems together because when one person  rose, everyone rose.
The justice system helps people better themselves and change their mentality

In the future, people will live in a world filled with justice, safety and peace.
Pursue justice
Respect one another/ mutual together
Ensure safety
